title: Never replay a brief on reconnect: wrapper forms and a shell for commands foreman cannot vouch for
body:
Review finding on commit 009024d (read its body and docs/remote-sessions.md). A REGRESSION: reconnect can now replay an agent's original brief. remote::relaunch reruns "its own command, arguments and all" for anything remote::program_agent refuses, and program_agent refuses common real agent launches: `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code "brief"`, `npx --yes ...`, `npx @openai/codex@latest ...`, `wsl -d Ubuntu -- claude "brief"`, and wrappers such as `env X=1 codex "brief"`, `nice claude "brief"`, `sudo -u x claude "brief"`, `bash -c 'claude "brief"'`. Before 009024d those relaunched a bare provider with no brief. Now a dropped Dispatch that the human reconnects restarts the agent with the same brief and it redoes the work. The spec's rule is that a reconnect never replays the original prompt; 009024d also dropped that rule from the docs.
The human's standing requirement: proven by driving the real application; reproduce BEFORE the fix, verify AFTER, record both, the same way as 009024d (its card: `foreman kanban list 2icttw --json`; reuse its setup: own release builds under target/agent/, config dir target/agent/appdata-s2hp4s restored afterwards, own pipe, test Remote andy@192.168.8.168 key login, a new /tmp directory per run, clean up what you create, never stop a foreman by name, install nothing on the Remote).
Blocked by: Reconnect and restore a Remote pane by its real program, not a name it mentions
Fix, both parts:
A. program_agent understands the option forms of the two wrappers it already accepts, and nothing more: npx with -y / --yes / -p or --package forms only if you can state their grammar exactly, and an @version or @tag suffix on the exact package names; wsl / wsl.exe with -d <distro>, -u <user>, --distribution, --user, -e / --exec and `--`. Unknown flags mean refuse. Look up the real grammar (npx --help, wsl --help from this PC) rather than guessing, and cite what you used in a comment. Also refuse `npx claude` / `npx codex` if those bare names are different npm packages from the real CLIs (check the registry; say what you found), and decide deliberately about argv[0] stems with an extension that is not an executable's (codex.py, claude.sh, grok.md must not be agents; claude.exe and claude.cmd on a Windows Remote must be).
B. Reconnect never replays arguments it cannot vouch for. Three classes, one pure function, one table test:
   1. program_agent says agent: resume as today (claude --continue, codex resume --last; an accepted wrapper relaunches the bare provider fresh).
   2. the command does not mention any agent name anywhere (plain `vi notes.md`, `htop`, `tail -f app.log`, a shell): rerun it as it was, as today.
   3. the command mentions an agent name but program_agent refuses it (env X=1 codex "brief", nice claude "brief", bash -c 'claude "brief"', but also vi codex.md and tail -f grok.log): foreman cannot tell a brief from a file name, so the reconnect opens a Remote login shell in the same directory and runs nothing. The disconnect bar and the reconnect banner must say so before the human presses Enter (wording in the bar's existing style, for example "Enter to reconnect to a shell"), and the banner prints the original command so the human can rerun it themselves.
   The mention test for class 3 may reuse the icon's scan (icons::IconKind::from_argv) as a pure "is an agent name mentioned" question; it must never again decide what to run or type.
   Restore `reconnect never replays an agent's original prompt` to docs/remote-sessions.md with these three classes, and correct both providers' dispatch skill copies if they describe reconnect (embedded-skill rebuild rule in foreman-docs-and-writing).
Also: the Remote's "needs login" row should still clear when a real agent opens through an accepted wrapper (it goes through program_agent now; confirm with a test).
Reproduce live BEFORE (main as it is): on the Remote open `env FOO=1 claude "<brief that makes Claude post one distinctive word to the room>"` in a trusted throwaway directory (answer the trust dialog once yourself), let it post, stop its ssh child on this PC by PID, `foreman reconnect`, and show the brief runs again (second post, or the transcript's second user turn). AFTER: the same steps end at a login shell in that directory, nothing run, the bar and banner wording captured from snapshot. Also AFTER: `vi codex.md` reconnects to a shell (not Codex, not vi), a plain `vi notes.md` reconnects to vi, and a real Claude resumes (claude --continue) and posts on the new token. If npx can launch the real Claude on the Remote without installing anything new, verify one accepted npx form resumes bare; if it would download a package, do not run it: unit tests only, and say so.
Hard rules as before: nothing assumes foreman on the Remote; a Remote agent's allowed actions are unchanged; no wire change; nothing under cfg(test) spawns a process or socket outside the remote_probe network guard; do not change icons::IconKind::from_argv or the tab icon; do not type into or answer any Codex update prompt.
Done when:
- one pure function gives the reconnect class with a table test covering every row named above plus the rows of the existing typed_route and relaunch tables
- BEFORE and AFTER observed on the real Remote and recorded in the commit body and a short spec Results entry
- docs and skill copies state the three classes; cite-guard clean; full suite passes; cargo fmt leaves nothing uncommitted
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
